reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it depicts boxing-event coverage focused on April Jay Abne, a championship trophy, and post-match interactions. The merchandise, subscription options, and conditional free workout offer are described as ordinary channel-support or promotional terms, and the available video evidence identifies no established payment, data-collection, deception, or harmful-destination mechanism.

citations.quote: April Jay Abne | New Ubs Flyweight Champion | A Real Underdog Story | Want to be an artist!
SUPPORT OUR CHANNEL and Buy Official Powcast Shirt Merchandise

opening.argument: Judge, the free workout is presented as a reward for taking specific steps, not merely as background information: viewers are told to subscribe, show the video, and identify a referral contact. The offer gives the audience a concrete reason to move from watching sports coverage into a claimed benefit. The description does not establish what happens when a viewer attempts to redeem it, so the promise-action linkage deserves scrutiny even though the requested action is simple.

citations.quote: ARE YOU POWCAST SUBSCRIBER? GET 1 FREE BOXING OR MMA WORKOUT Session at MUMMA Fight Club Gym in Makati,Philippines. Just Subscribe to Powcast Sports and show them this video.
Look for Elly/ [PHONE] and tell them you were referred by #Powcast

rebuttal.rebuttal: The boxing footage and championship framing establish the subject of the video, but they do not resolve the separate offer in its description. Calling the workout terms ordinary promotion assumes the promised session can be obtained on those terms; the supplied material states the steps but does not verify redemption. The question is whether that free-benefit solicitation should be treated as incidental merely because it accompanies genuine sports coverage.

citations.quote: Just Subscribe to Powcast Sports and show them this video.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description openly names the gym and says exactly what a viewer must do for the session. Nothing supplied shows a hidden charge, a false promise, or a failed redemption. A conditional promotional offer alongside footage of a boxing event does not become a scam solely because its fulfillment is not independently documented here.

citations.quote: GET 1 FREE BOXING OR MMA WORKOUT Session at MUMMA Fight Club Gym in Makati,Philippines. Just Subscribe to Powcast Sports and show them this video.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the offer in the context of the description's other calls to action. The same description promises a free workout for subscribers, directs viewers to a named referral contact, asks for Patreon pledges, and lists affiliate stores. Each item is disclosed, but together they make the description a network of participation and off-video destinations. The free claim is the easiest entry point; the supplied material does not show what terms a viewer encounters after acting on it. That uncertainty matters when assessing the solicitation, even without assuming any particular charge or outcome.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the merchandise and subscription requests as ordinary promotions, but disclosure of several destinations does not establish the terms encountered at any of them. Its reliance on the absence of an established harmful destination also leaves the free workout's redemption untested. The cumulative issue is the combination of a free-benefit claim, referral instruction, and other participation requests, not proof that any listed destination has already caused harm.

citations.quote: GET 1 FREE BOXING OR MMA WORKOUT Session at MUMMA Fight Club Gym in Makati,Philippines.
Look for Elly/ [PHONE] and tell them you were referred by #Powcast

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Grouping disclosed promotions does not supply the missing evidence of deception. The description identifies the workout conditions, labels the stores as affiliates, and separately asks for voluntary Patreon support. No supplied source shows that these are stages of one misleading offer or that the free session requires a purchase. Multiple ordinary calls to action do not, by accumulation alone, establish a scam.

opening.argument: Judge, the sports presentation also functions as a route into the description's offer. The title foregrounds a new flyweight champion and an underdog story, while the footage shows a boxing-ring celebration. That gives viewers a reason to watch and to trust the channel's proximity to the sport. The description then addresses subscribers with a free boxing or MMA workout, requiring them to show this video and give a referral name. The sports content can be genuine and still serve a promotional purpose: here, the promised benefit is explicitly tied to viewer action.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the frames depict boxing coverage. That does not make the description's request irrelevant: it expressly tells viewers to use this video when seeking the free session. The championship story and the workout solicitation are linked by the publisher's own instructions, so the promotional function should be assessed alongside the sports footage rather than dismissed as unrelated.

citations.quote: Just Subscribe to Powcast Sports and show them this video.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The footage and title support a straightforward sports story. The description's workout offer may promote the channel, but promotion is not itself deception. Its stated conditions are visible, and the supplied evidence does not show that the channel's sports coverage conceals a false offer or redirects viewers into a harmful transaction.
